In case you are looking for more ways to learn R, here are a couple more things
to look at:

+ The Carpentries offers a lot of materials for learning R, including:
  + A thorough lesson on [R programming for reproducible analyses](https://swcarpentry.github.io/r-novice-gapminder)
  + Data analyses and visualization in [R for ecologists](https://datacarpentry.org/R-ecology-lesson/)
  + Data analyses and visualization in [R for social scientists](https://datacarpentry.org/r-socialsci/)
  + Working with [geospatial data in R](https://datacarpentry.org/r-raster-vector-geospatial)
+ IBM Data Scientist Kelsey Gonzalez's [lessons on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL6FsZxVq54ERrlMRNE5aq2qUFH042fbuM)
